name: Shemaiah the Nehelamite
charge: Sending letters in his own name from Babylon to have Jeremiah put in prison and in the stocks as a madman; prophesying when the Lord sent him not, and causing the people to trust in a lie
summary: Shemaiah the Nehelamite, among the captives in Babylon, sent letters in his own name to Jerusalem and to Zephaniah the priest, demanding to know why Jeremiah had not been put in the stocks as a madman for writing that the captivity would be long (Jeremiah 29:24-28). Zephaniah read the letter to Jeremiah, and the word came back that Shemaiah prophesied when the Lord had not sent him and made the people trust in a lie; he and his seed would have no man among the people and would not see the good the Lord would do (Jeremiah 29:29-32).
offenseFull: Jeremiah had written to the captives carried away with Jeconiah that they would be in Babylon seventy years, and must build, plant, marry and seek the peace of the city (Jeremiah 29:4-10). The Zedekiah teaching explains the setting: Ezekiel was among the captives, messengers went back and forth, and false prophets were telling the captives they would soon return, when the word was that they would serve Babylon seventy years. Shemaiah the Nehelamite was one of them. The teacher gives the name as meaning dreamer, which sets him with the prophets of Jeremiah 23 who said they had dreamed when the Lord had not shown them anything (Jeremiah 23:25-27).

He sent letters in his own name to all the people at Jerusalem, to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests (Jeremiah 29:25). He told Zephaniah the Lord had made him priest in place of Jehoiada, to be an officer in the house of the Lord over every man who is mad and makes himself a prophet, to put him in prison and in the stocks, and asked why he had not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who made himself a prophet and had sent to Babylon saying the captivity would be long, so build houses and plant gardens (Jeremiah 29:26-28). He wrote in his own name, not the Lord’s, and wanted the prophet who told the truth locked up as a madman. The study note marks the difference between the two men: the Lord was dealing with Jeremiah.

The long captivity was the offence. It was seventy years at that time, one teacher says, and now it is hundreds. The letter Shemaiah attacked told the captives to settle because the Lord had set the time, and to fight it, another teacher says, is to fight the Most High.
judgmentFull: Zephaniah read the letter in Jeremiah’s hearing, and the word came to Jeremiah to send to all the captivity: because Shemaiah had prophesied to them when the Lord had not sent him, and made them trust in a lie, the Lord would punish him and his seed; none of his line would live among the people, and he would not see the good the Lord would do for His people, because he had taught rebellion against the Lord (Jeremiah 29:29-32). His sentence reached his seed as well as himself. The study note names his offence with the same words as Hananiah’s: he taught rebellion (Jeremiah 28:16), leading the people against the time the Lord had set instead of accepting that they had to go through captivity.

The good he would not see is the good the letter promised: after seventy years the Lord would visit His people and bring them back, for His plans toward them were for peace and not for harm, to give them a hopeful end (Jeremiah 29:10-11). The class of 2026-05-23 takes that end as the comfort of the captivity: everything you see here is temporary, and you already know the end. The teaching on the letter says the prophets understood the time, and in that was their patience and their hope (Jeremiah 29:12-14). The false prophets offered a quick return; the true word offered a sure one, and Shemaiah was cut off from it.

text.text: Thus shalt thou also speak to Shemaiah the Nehelamite, saying,

Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, saying, Because thou hast sent letters in thy name unto all the people that are at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

The Lord hath made thee priest in the stead of Jehoiada the priest, that ye should be officers in the house of the Lord, for every man that is mad, and maketh himself a prophet, that thou shouldest put him in prison, and in the stocks.
Now therefore why hast thou not reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet to you?
For therefore he sent unto us in Babylon, saying, This captivity is long: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.
And Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then came the word of the Lord unto Jeremiah, saying,

Send to all them of the captivity, saying, Thus saith the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite; Because that Shemaiah hath prophesied unto you, and I sent him not, and he caused you to trust in a lie:

Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite, and his seed: he shall not have a man to dwell among this people; neither shall he behold the good that I will do for my people, saith the Lord; because he hath taught rebellion against the Lord.
Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon;
Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them;

Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters; that ye may be increased there, and not diminished.
And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the Lord for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.
For thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Let not your prophets and your diviners, that be in the midst of you, deceive you, neither hearken to your dreams which ye cause to be dreamed.
For they prophesy falsely unto you in my name: I have not sent them, saith the Lord.
For thus saith the Lord, That after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.
I have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.
How long shall this be in the heart of the prophets that prophesy lies? yea, they are prophets of the deceit of their own heart;
Which think to cause my people to forget my name by their dreams which they tell every man to his neighbour, as their fathers have forgotten my name for Baal.

Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, saying, Because thou hast sent letters in thy name unto all the people that are at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

The Lord hath made thee priest in the stead of Jehoiada the priest, that ye should be officers in the house of the Lord, for every man that is mad, and maketh himself a prophet, that thou shouldest put him in prison, and in the stocks.
Now therefore why hast thou not reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet to you?
For therefore he sent unto us in Babylon, saying, This captivity is long: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.
Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the earth: this year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the Lord.
For thus saith the Lord, That after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
Then shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you.
And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.

And I will be found of you, saith the Lord: and I will turn away your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places whither I have driven you, saith the Lord; and I will bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive.
